recommendation: Keep this no-change audit. If implementers need a jurisdiction-specific or X12-specific filing-indicator code system, represent it through profiles or terminology guidance using Claim.supportingInfo category/code rather than changing core Claim for this historical issue.
issue_request: FHIR-7323 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Claim change request from DSTU1 asking for a filing indicator such as L&I or MVA; the resolution recorded that this had already been added in STU3 as Claim.information.
initial_application: No Claim source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-7323 was found. The relevant historical application appears in the 2016 Claim WGM update that added Claim.information with an InformationCategory binding and accident/employment categories; later Claim maintenance renamed Claim.information to Claim.supportingInfo under FHIR-19460.
additional_context: Claim is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current version mapping records Claim.information=Claim.supportingInfo. The active Claim definition includes Claim.supportingInfo for exceptions, special considerations, conditions, situations, and prior or concurrent issues; its category definition explicitly includes accident and employment; and item lines can link to supporting information by sequence. Community searches found no direct FHIR-7323 Zulip or Confluence record and no conflicting work-group evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. Current active source already preserves the resolved Claim.information capability under its current Claim.supportingInfo name, so adding another core Claim element or prose statement would be redundant.

related_jiras.note: Renamed Claim.information to Claim.supportingInfo to align with the Request pattern, explaining why the original resolution now appears under a different element name.
